topics.topic: Boundary and representation for rejecting duplicate JSON object keys
questions: How can canonical_bytes detect duplicate object keys after its input has already become a JSON value, and which layer must reject them?
At what boundary and from what representation are duplicate JSON object keys detected, given that an ordinary parsed JSON value no longer preserves them?

judgement.why: This asks the same canonical-JSON input-boundary and duplicate-member-detection question already decided by P1, and the relevant passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Input boundary for canonical JSON bytes and duplicate-member detection
quotes: canonical_bytes: [BEHAVIOR] MUST parse json_text as one JSON value and emit its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form encoded as UTF-8: object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names, numbers written in the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (an integral double without a fraction or exponent, so a number written 1.0 becomes 1), strings escaped exactly as JCS prescribes, and no whitespace; it applies no Unicode normalization, so two texts that differ only in normalization give different bytes.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.

translate_failure: [FIELD_PROJECTION] Maps a failure to its code of = models.RefusalCode: UnknownReferenceError to unknown_reference, RefusedError to refused, InvalidRequestError and NonCanonicalValueError to invalid_request; StoreInternalError, StopRequiredError and every other exception to internal_error.
precedent.why: State 7 makes canonical_bytes parse raw JSON text, detect duplicate members, and maps its error to invalid_request.

topics.topic: First-start creation and private-directory requirements for open_store
questions: Does open_store create and initialize a new store, require a pre-created empty directory, or refuse missing store components?

If the configured data directory, database, or required subdirectories do not yet exist, does open_store create them or refuse, and what ownership and permission conditions exactly constitute a private directory?

judgement.divergence: One implementer creates a missing data_directory with private ownership and permissions before initializing the database and subdirectories; another refuses startup because the configured data_directory does not already exist. The installer or owner notices whether a first start succeeds and creates the store or fails.
judgement.why: The later text says absent database schema, content-addressed area and spool area are created, and defines privacy for an existing data_directory, but never decides whether the data_directory itself is created or required to preexist.

topics.topic: Outcome when a successful trial or admission value exceeds the storage limit
questions: What happens when an otherwise successful trial or admission execution returns a value output larger than stored_value_bytes_max?
How does a try or admission conclude when a sandbox-successful value output exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max` and therefore cannot be kept as the required StoredValue?

quotes: execute_trial_case: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is the sandbox outcome of the same name; a succeeded execution is passed when the case has no expected outputs or every output's digest equals the expected one, a many file output equal only with the same length and equal digests position by position, and output_mismatch otherwise; a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant makes the outcome contract_violation.

execute_trial_case: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] For passed and output_mismatch the outputs are recorded, a value as a StoredValue stored with put_value_bytes and a file by digest, size and media type only as a FileFactsRef whose disclosure_class is the highest class of the case's inputs, every output taking that class; other outcomes record outputs None; one RecordTrialExecutionChange is written through record_change with resources_used, the sandbox's detail_code (value_too_large for an output over the stored value ceiling), the sandbox's failure_detail, executed_at from kernel_now and the given actor.
judgement.why: The later notes make an oversized successful value output a contract_violation with no recorded outputs and detail code value_too_large for both try and admission through execute_trial_case.

topics.topic: Startup validation scope for installed service manifests and capabilities
questions: Which operation-independent manifest checks are performed at startup, and are all capability entries validated or only record and selected-instance structure?
Which A08 checks are applied to a service manifest during startup, and are per-operation capability entries validated when no operation or proposal is named?

quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
judgement.why: The later notes restrict startup validation to read_service_record's operation-independent record checks and the selected instance's credential-header collision, without invoking per-operation capability validation.
